method: Implements single-byte code page conversion as a direct 256-entry table lookup. Each page maps byte values 0x00–0xFF to one Unicode code point taken from the published mappings for IBM CP437 and CP850 (printable range 0x20–0xFF), Microsoft Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1, and EBCDIC CP037 and CP500; the six tables were generated from those reference mappings and every defined byte was verified to round-trip back to its own value before release. Encoding walks the input by Unicode code point and writes one byte per character, substituting 0x3F (question mark) for any character the selected page cannot represent and reporting both the count and the first five positions, so a substitution is never silent. Bytes 0x00–0x1F and 0x7F keep their C0 and delete code points rather than the graphic glyphs a DOS screen or 3270 terminal may draw for those positions. Decoding accepts two-digit hexadecimal bytes with optional whitespace, rejects non-hexadecimal characters, incomplete pairs and more than 4,096 bytes, and renders the five undefined Windows-1252 bytes 0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90 and 0x9D as U+FFFD instead of guessing a character. Input is limited to 4,096 characters or bytes. There is no charset auto-detection, transliteration, multi-byte or DBCS code page support, encryption, or network access, and the tool does not claim a page is correct for an unknown source system.
